 Spurs have a bench warmer who will block Williams-Barnett's pathway
 Originally posted on
 Football FanCast 
  | 
 By Angus Sinclair
  | 
 Last updated Nov 20, 2026 2:10 AM ET
 Add us as a preferred source on Google
 Mauricio Pochettino is back in the Premier League , but he won't be taking charge of Tottenham Hotspur , who were linked with then USMNT manager before pursuing Roberto De Zerbi .
 The new Manchester United boss will be hoping to rebuild a system of the kind which drew Spurs away from their languishing position and established them as one of the strongest and most attractive teams in the Premier League. 
 Had Tottenham moved for their old boss, a certain romance would have arrived in tow, but De Zerbi was a fresh face, and while it's not been perfect, there's no question that the Italian has overseen a few improvements down N17.
 How De Zerbi is improving Spurs 
 De Zerbi was not the architect of Tottenham's expensive summer transfer window, but he would have played an important role, and after some early teething problems, has hammered the squad into a state of tactical fluency.
 "I think Spurs fans can really get behind this team now"Jamie Redknapp on Roberto De Zerbi changing the mentality of Tottenham âšª pic.twitter.com/5UbPRaH7xs — Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) October 24, 2026 
 Back-to-back 17th-place finishes have chagrined this proud football, but, despite losing at Leeds United before the international break, Tottenham have risen from that lowly position and trail fifth-place Chelsea by six places, but only four points.
 Defensively, the Londoners are still a tad rusty, but De Zerbi has shaped big-money midfield additions Sandro Tonali and Rodrigo Bentancur into crucial cogs at the heart of the engine. Only Manchester City have seen more of the ball than Spurs.

 Moreover, Tottenham are striking a welcome balance between experience and youthful avidity. Luca Williams-Barnett is the perfect example of the latter.
 Why William-Barnett is so special 
 When looking at the Premier League's most exciting youngsters, Rio Ngumoha and Max Dowman are presently regarded as the cream of the crop. But Williams-Barnett could soon enter that conversation, with Steven Gerrard recently calling him Tottenham's " own little Ngumoha ".
 REUTERS/Scott Heppell
 He plays with a fearlessness that has been markedly absent down N17 over the past several years. The academy product is capable of creating magic when on the ball, and fashioned a glorious chance for Mohammed Kudus in the late stages against Crystal Palace at the end of October. The Ghanaian squandered that opportunity. 
 A vibrant and attack-focused player who still hasn't cemented their strongest position, the 18-year-old has technical quality in abundance, but he also has character and spirit and determination.
 REUTERS/Dylan Martinez
 In Pochettino, Spurs could have re-hired a manager with wherewithal and a track record of promoting youth. He might have been perfect for Williams-Barnett's development.
 Even so, De Zerbi is doing a fine job, easing the teenager onto the major stage.
 Spurs star could keep Williams-Barnett on the fringes 
 Williams-Barnett has a part to play over the coming years at Tottenham, but there's a case to be made that a year out on loan might benefit him - and Spurs - in the long run.
 After all, Williams-Barnett's emergence has coincided with Dejan Kulusevski's return from an interminable injury. The Swedish attacking midfielder is hardly fit and firing once again, but he's playing, and De Zerbi believes he will play a focal role as his recovery continues.
 The 26-year-old has played four times in the Premier League this season. He has not started a game, but has looked strong and steady when dribbling, completing three of four dribbles thus far.
 We've yet to see the return of Kulusevski's creative brilliance - in that regard he's perhaps their finest creator since the days of Christian Eriksen . 
 Indeed, he was once hailed as a " world-class talent " by football scout Jacek Kulig, and if he recovers his form, there's no question that Williams-Barnett may find minutes hard to come by in an uncertain and shaky Spurs side. Linked with a move away too, the Swede's return could be the final nail in the coffin for the teenager's Tottenham career.
 Kulusevski missed 526 days of football due to a patella injury that encountered complication after complication during the recovery process. He is a fantastic footballer, so often a breath of fresh air during those earlier days of his Spurs career. Will he return to that one-time level? Surpass it? Time will tell, but De Zerbi clearly thinks it's worth guiding him back into the run of things.
 Action Images via Reuters/Paul Childs
 Let's not forget: James Maddison is finding form this season, having featured only once last year. Moreover, Xavi Simons continues to recuperate on the sidelines, and his return to prove another complication for Williams-Barnett to navigate at this early stage. 
 There's no question that the young attacker has a bright future in north London, but De Zerbi and co have faith in Kulusevski's chances of making a successful return to his former level, and if that does happen, Williams-Barnett will need to wait a while yet before becoming a mainstay at Tottenham.
